mbm-1976.clue: The little wheel really goes round.
mbm-1976.quote: I put a Ferris wheel on our fairground quilt and fastened its center with a smooth old button. My cousin turns the cars to put her favorite one at the top before bed.

mbm-1977.clue: I quilt the rainy days in yellow.
mbm-1977.quote: My dad worked outdoors and only played cards with us on rainy afternoons. I stitched our old deck as patches. The sunniest squares in the blanket stand for the days he was home.

mbm-1978.clue: My sketch has an extra carriage.
mbm-1978.quote: I drew the night train through a rainy window. One lit window reflected in my tea, so I put a tiny carriage at the bottom of the page. It travels wherever my cup goes.

mbm-1979.clue: We found the square with our eyes shut.
mbm-1979.quote: My friend described the sounds in her old holiday postcards. We followed the bell, then the fountain, then the squeaky green gate. When we opened our eyes we were at her grandfather's courtyard.

mbm-1980.clue: My screen saver has a night shift.
mbm-1980.quote: I made little window cleaners wash the desktop when the computer is idle. At midnight one of them sits on the sill with a sandwich. I stayed up to make sure he took his break.

mbm-1981.clue: I ran five minutes slower for a good reason.
mbm-1981.quote: When a neighbor's wind-up clock stops he sets it by my morning run. I stopped to tie my lace and tell him the correct time. We had a biscuit before I started the clock again.

mbm-1982.clue: I know that voice by its pencil.
mbm-1982.quote: My radio friend drops his pencil every time he leans across the dial. I heard the little clatter at a club meet and turned around before he said his name.

mbm-1983.clue: I hold the sketchbook upside down for the loop.
mbm-1983.quote: At the air display my niece drew the smoke trails while I drew the planes. To get the loop just right we turned the book right round between our hands. There are two laughing faces in the margins.

mbm-1984.clue: I write my pirates on a grocery list.
mbm-1984.quote: I ran out of paper on the train and gave a pirate a speech between the milk and the onions. Back home Grandpa bought everything, including a perfectly good compass.

mbm-1985.clue: I ate my way through a drawbridge.
mbm-1985.quote: The fair's gingerbread contest counted how many shapes you finished. The last biscuit was a drawbridge with two little chains of icing. I ate the chains first. According to my nephew, the rest fell in the moat.

mbm-1986.clue: I can quilt a square with one finger.
mbm-1986.quote: When my grandmother's hands got tired, she traced a star in spilled flour and I cut pieces to match. That wobbly flour star is in the center of our best blanket.

mbm-1987.clue: The flag has my uncle's handwriting.
mbm-1987.quote: We made a putting hole in the garden and tied an old white hankie to the pin. His laundry initials are just visible in the corner. Whenever I sink a long one the little letters wave.

mbm-1988.clue: I like a cuff that gives you directions.
mbm-1988.quote: I sewed a scrap of the local bus map inside my brother's raincoat. If he turns back his sleeve he can find the stop for home without taking off his gloves.

mbm-1989.clue: The tiny house on the edge is waiting.
mbm-1989.quote: I made a quilt of our street before my cousin's house was built. I left one plain green block and a little cardboard house in my sewing tin. When she got the keys, the house moved in.

mbm-1990.clue: My program measures how long a joke lasts.
mbm-1990.quote: I gave the pixel audience in my first comedy game three different laughs. Dad held down the big button until they fell out of their seats. I had to write them some sturdier chairs.

mbm-1991.clue: That chalk streak looks like a smile from below.
mbm-1991.quote: Halfway up the wall I slipped off a smooth hold and left two chalky handprints. From the mat they looked like a grin. I climbed back up the next day just to reach its nose.

mbm-1992.clue: I can name a tune by one loose string.
mbm-1992.quote: My old cuatro has a string that buzzes a little on damp evenings. My uncle wrote a bar of music that waits for the buzz. When the weather clears we play it the ordinary way.

mbm-1993.clue: I wrote a postcard to the sky.
mbm-1993.quote: After my first jump I drew the shape of our landing field on a postcard and mailed it to myself. It arrived on a gray day. I pinned that big green field over my desk.

mbm-1994.clue: The blanket fort has a concession stand.
mbm-1994.quote: For movie night my niece cut a ticket window in a cardboard box beside the sofa. I bring popcorn in my pajama pocket and she charges one enormous yawn for admission.

mbm-1995.clue: I don't need binoculars for the first arrival.
mbm-1995.quote: The little café beside our airfield sets a blue cup upside down on the wall when the first flight comes in. I sketched the cup for a whole winter before I finally drew the plane.

mbm-1996.clue: I brought a peach to a midnight showing.
mbm-1996.quote: Auntie and I used to share a peach on the cinema steps after the late show. On her birthday I bring one, split it around the stone, and take a long time over the good half.

mbm-1997.clue: Our club's dragon has a crooked horn.
mbm-1997.quote: We passed a dragon sketch round the room, each drawing one more scale. The fold in the paper bent his horn. Our clay model wears that horn crooked, too.

mbm-1998.clue: My story has a page that smells like orange.
mbm-1998.quote: I dropped orange peel between chapters and left a bright oil mark on the paper. I made it a clue for my kitchen detective. Now I've got a perfectly innocent fruit seller under suspicion.

mbm-1999.clue: I've stitched one mitten for every guest.
mbm-1999.quote: My grandmother's friends used to hang their mittens over her radiator. I made a row of mismatched mittens across her quilt. She knew every guest by the colors.

mbm-2000.clue: My flipbook waits for the train.
mbm-2000.quote: I drew our little anime hero staring at a station clock for twelve frames. In the last one his sandwich disappears. My club thought I'd forgotten a drawing. I told them to watch the cat.
